titleEn: Even in the Dark, I Can Hear Dad!

pages.text: "Dad, don't turn off the light!" Pongi called from under the blanket. The bridge lantern was lit outside. Dad, in his overalls, had just blown out the little lantern. The room was all dark. Pongi wanted to sleep with the light on.

Beside her, her little brother was already asleep with his shell. She looked at the wall. Oh! A long, pointy shadow stood there. It looked like a monster to Pongi. "What's that?" She squeezed her eyes shut and pulled the blanket to her nose.
Sniff! Hearing a sound from under the blanket, Dad tiptoed back. He sat on the floor beside the sofa and held Pongi's paws in his. "You were scared. I'm right here." Pongi opened her eyes a little.
Dad asked, "What scared you?" Pongi pointed to the wall. "There... the pointy monster." Dad turned toward the wall. "Then shall we go and see what it is together?"

Dad stood in front of the shadow. "It's my overalls hanging on the shelf!" The bridge lantern shone through the window and stretched the shadow out long. Pongi's mouth opened a little. "So it wasn't a monster?"

"Now let's look with our ears instead of our eyes." Dad walked through the dark room. Tap, tap. Pongi pricked up her ears. "I can hear! Dad, you're beside the table!" Dad smiled. "That's right. Even in the dark, I can hear Dad!"
This time, Pongi listened for each sound. Soft breathing. "My brother breathing!" Rippling water. "The water outside!" There was nothing scary. Pongi called, "Even in the dark, I can hear Dad!"

Pongi's heart wasn't thumping now. "Only the light went out. The room stayed the same!" The bridge lantern glowed round and bright in the window. Under her blanket, Pongi thumped her tail on the sofa.
In the dark room, Dad counted three things. "One, say, 'I'm scared!' Two, prick up your ears and listen! Three, hold the paw of the person beside you tight!" Pongi held Dad's paw even tighter.

Dad laid Pongi down and tucked the blanket over her. "Call if you're scared. Dad's voice is right here." Even with the light out, everything was still there. Pongi closed her eyes and whispered, "Even in the dark, I can hear Dad!"
